walkthrough:
**Identify the three pressure lines**

First, get your bearings. The solid line is ventricle pressure, the dotted line is aortic pressure, and the dashed line is atrial pressure. Valves always respond to which side has the higher pressure.

Remember the rule: blood flows from high to low pressure, and valves prevent backflow.

**Recall the valve rules**

This is the key biology. The atrioventricular (AV) valves close when $P_{ventricle} > P_{atrium}$, so blood cannot go back into the atria. The semilunar valves open when $P_{ventricle} > P_{aorta}$, so blood can be ejected into the aorta.

**Apply the rules to period C**

In period C, the solid line is right at the top. Ventricle pressure is higher than both aortic pressure and atrial pressure. That means $P_{ventricle} > P_{aorta}$ so semilunar valves are open, and $P_{ventricle} > P_{atrium}$ so AV valves are held shut. This is ventricular ejection, so the answer is C.

options.A: In A, atrial pressure is slightly above ventricle pressure. This is atrial systole, so AV valves are open and semilunar valves are closed.
options.B: In B, ventricle pressure is rising sharply but is still at or below aortic pressure. This is isovolumetric contraction with both sets of valves closed.
options.C: In C, ventricle pressure exceeds both aortic and atrial pressure. Semilunar valves are forced open for ejection while AV valves are held closed.
options.D: In D, ventricle pressure falls rapidly below aortic pressure. Semilunar valves close, and as ventricle pressure drops below atrial pressure the AV valves open for filling.
